title: Freelancer Tool Subscriptions and Irregular Income
metaDescription: Budget around uneven client payments, track software and AI tool subscriptions and UPI AutoPay, and keep advance tax dates in one manual list.
h1: How do freelancers in India track tool subscriptions when income arrives in lumps?
summary: Freelancers in India face two money problems at once: client payments arrive irregularly, while software tools, cloud storage and AI subscriptions bill every month whether or not a project came in. A manual tracker such as Essara lets you log income as it arrives, list every tool with its renewal date, and set a monthly budget with a daily spending limit, without linking your bank account.
stepsHeading: Set up your tool and income list

sections.heading: Budgeting when income is irregular
paragraphs: A fixed monthly tool bill looks harmless in a good month and painful in a slow one. The fix is to plan from the bottom, not the average. Look at your lowest recent month of income, and make sure that month still covers your fixed tool costs, rent and essentials. Anything above that goes into a buffer, so a quiet quarter does not force you to cancel the tools you depend on.

Essara's monthly budget shows what is left to spend and a daily spending limit, which is useful when your income is uneven. Log income on the day a client pays rather than the day you expected it, so the budget reflects cash you actually have.

sections.heading: Tools that outlive the project
paragraphs: Tools are easy to start and hard to remember. A design app bought for one client, a cloud plan you upgraded during a launch, or an AI assistant you stopped using in March can keep billing. The cheapest habit is a single list of every tool with its cycle, renewal date and the project it served, reviewed once a quarter.

Check each store's subscription list as well as your card statement, because a tool billed through Google Play or the App Store will not always stand out in a statement. Cancelling happens in that store or vendor account, not in Essara, so mark each entry 'business' or 'personal' in its name to keep the two visible side by side.

sections.heading: Tools billed through UPI AutoPay
paragraphs: Some hosting plans and tools bill through UPI AutoPay, which is easy to miss because nothing appears in your card statement. In Google Pay, open Autopay from your profile picture and use the Live tab to pause or cancel a mandate with your UPI PIN. Google's help page notes that a mandate above ₹15,000 asks for your UPI PIN again each time a payment is due.
Cancelling the mandate stops future debits, but it does not end the tool itself, so do both. If you cannot see the Autopay section, update Google Pay.

sections.heading: Advance tax and the renewal calendar
paragraphs: If your total tax for the year is ₹10,000 or more after TDS and TCS, advance tax generally applies to freelancers as well as salaried people. For most individuals the schedule is 15% of the year's tax by 15 June, 45% by 15 September, 75% by 15 December and 100% by 15 March, less amounts already paid. Those rules moved into the Income-tax Act, 2025, which applies from 1 April 2026, so older articles that cite section 211 of the 1961 Act are out of date. Presumptive-scheme taxpayers have different rules.

Add each advance tax date to your tracker as a bill with a reminder, next to your tool renewals, so the cash for them is planned before the date arrives. Confirm your own schedule on the income tax portal before paying, as the portal is the authority on current instalments.

steps.name: Pull three months of charges
steps.text: Check Google Play and Apple subscriptions, the Autopay section of your UPI app and your card statement for every tool you pay for.

steps.name: Create your account
steps.text: Sign up at essara.space/signup, or install the Android app from Google Play. The same account works on Android and the web app, including the installable web app on iPhone.

steps.name: Add each tool with its cycle
steps.text: Enter the name, amount, billing cycle and next renewal date. Put 'business' or 'personal' in the name so you can tell them apart.

steps.name: Add UPI AutoPay mandates
steps.text: Copy each mandate from your UPI app's Autopay list, so tool debits appear with the rest of your renewals.

steps.name: Log your income as it arrives
steps.text: Record each client payment as income on the day it lands, not the day you expected it.

steps.name: Set a budget from your lowest month
steps.text: Set the monthly budget from your lowest recent month, then check left-to-spend and the daily spending limit.

steps.name: Scan a tool invoice
steps.text: Scan one tool bill with the receipt scanner, review the merchant, total and date, then save. The free plan includes 5 scans a month.

faqs.q: Does Essara create invoices or handle GST?
faqs.a: No. Essara is an expense, subscription and budget tracker. Its listed features cover manual expense and income entry, renewal reminders, budgets, a daily spending limit, a receipt scanner and investment tracking. It does not list invoicing or GST filing, so keep those in your own tools.

faqs.q: How much should a freelancer keep as a monthly budget?
faqs.a: A safe starting point is your lowest recent month of income, after fixed tool costs and essentials are covered. Anything above that can go into a buffer. Revisit the figure each quarter as your client mix changes.

faqs.q: Can I stop a UPI AutoPay tool subscription from Google Pay?
faqs.a: Yes. Open Autopay in Google Pay, go to the Live tab, choose the mandate and tap Pause autopay or Cancel autopay, then enter your UPI PIN. You should still cancel the tool itself in its own account, because stopping the debit alone may not end the subscription.

faqs.q: Do freelancers have to pay advance tax?
faqs.a: If your total tax liability for the year, after TDS and TCS, is ₹10,000 or more, advance tax generally applies. Most individuals pay it in instalments by 15 June, 15 September, 15 December and 15 March. Check the current rules and your own schedule on the income tax portal before you pay.
